proposal

Erica Cai

Source: vignettes/proposal.qmd

Project 1 (Data: NHANES data from the NHANES package)

1. Research Question

Is BMI associated with diabetes status among adults aged 40 and older?

2. Unit of Analysis and population

Unit of Analysis: Individual within the US National Center for Health Statistics survey

Population: Adults aged 40 and older in the US

3. Exposure Variable

Definition: BMI: Body mass index (weight/height2 in kg/m2). It is a measure of weight relative to height. It is used to assess weight status and screen for underweight, overweight, and obesity.

How to code it: It is a continuous variable so I will use its original numerical values. Participants with missing BMI will be excluded.

4. Outcome Variable

Definition: Diabetes: Study participant told by a doctor or health professional that they have diabetes, indicating whether the participant has diabetes or not

Variable Type: Binary categorical variable

How to code it: Yes = 1 (diagnosed diabetes), No = 0 (not diagnosed diabetes). Participants with missing Diabetes will be excluded.

5. Confounders

Age: Age can affect the risk of diabetes and BMI due to age-related change of metabolism

Income: Higher income may provide better access to healthcare and healthier food , which may influence both BMI and diabetes risk.

Gender: Gender may be associated with both BMI and diabetes due to difference of hormone

Project 2 (Data: CDC data on waterborne illnesses)

1. Research Question

How is water exposure associated with the number of illness?

2. Unit of Analysis and population

Unit of Analysis: Individual waterborne disease event

Population: Waterbrone disease events in the US

3. Exposure Variable

Definition: water_exposure: Types of water, including drinking water, Other/environmental water and undetermined water

How to code it: It is a categorical variable so I will use its original categorical values. Event with missing water exposure type will be excluded.

4. Outcome Variable

Definition: illnesses: introducing the number of illnesses of the disease event

Variable Type: Discrete numerical variable

How to code it: I will use its original numerical values. Events with missing illnesses value will be excluded.

5. Confounders

Geography(State): Different areas may have different water condition and the overall environmental conditions, which may affect the water exposure type and number of illnesses

Time(Month): In different months, the environmental factors, such as weather, and human factors, such as daily activities, will be changes, which may affect the water exposure type and number of illnesses
